Start, stop and inspect the Julia session

lm_start.Rd

All computations run in one persistent Julia process. lm_start() launches it (through JuliaConnectoR), sets the number of Julia threads used for random starts and bootstrap replications, and loads LatentMixtures.jl and the package's bridge module once, so later calls do not pay the start-up and compilation cost again. lm_end() shuts the process down; lm_status() reports on it.

Usage

lm_start(threads = "auto", quiet = FALSE)

lm_end()

lm_status()

# S3 method for class 'lm_status'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

threads

Number of Julia threads (a positive integer), or "auto" (one per CPU core). Only used when Julia is started by this call.

quiet

Logical; suppress the start-up message.

x

An lm_status object.

...

Ignored.

Value

lm_start() (invisibly) and lm_status(): an object of class lm_status, a list with components

running

logical, whether a Julia process is connected;

ready

logical, whether LatentMixtures.jl and the bridge are loaded in it;

threads

integer, Julia threads of the running process (NA if not ready);

session

integer, the session identifier (see lm_session_id());

julia_version

character, the Julia version (NA if not ready);

threads_setting

character, the current value of JULIA_NUM_THREADS (NA if unset).

lm_end(): invisibly, TRUE if a running session was stopped, FALSE otherwise. The print() method returns x invisibly.

Details

Automatic start. Every fitting function starts the session when it is not running, with the threads given by the environment variable JULIA_NUM_THREADS if it is set (any syntax Julia accepts, e.g. "4,1"), otherwise "auto". Call lm_start() explicitly to choose the thread count or to pay the start-up cost up front.

Threads. Random starts (stage 1 and stage 2 of starts) and the bootstrap samples of blrt() are distributed over Julia threads. The thread count of a running Julia process cannot be changed: use lm_end(); lm_start(threads = n). If lm_start() is called while the session is running with a different count it warns and keeps the running session.

Shared process. JuliaConnectoR runs one Julia process per R session, shared with other packages (for example latentclasscausal). If a Julia process was already started by another package, lm_start() reuses it and its thread count.

Ending a session. Models fitted before lm_end() hold references to Julia objects that no longer exist. Printing them still works (the fit statistics are stored in R), but functions that need the Julia object (for example parameters(), classify(), r3step()) stop with a request to refit. The session identifier (lm_session_id()) is incremented at each start, so stale models are detected.

See also

install_julia_packages() to install the Julia packages; lm_session_id(); latentmixtures-package for the architecture.

Examples

lm_status()      # does not start Julia
#> Julia is not running; lm_start() starts it (fitting functions do so automatically)
# \donttest{
# start Julia explicitly (fitting functions also do this on first use)
lm_start(threads = 4)
#> Starting Julia ...
#> Julia 1.12.5 started with 4 threads; LatentMixtures.jl loaded.
lm_status()    # Julia version, threads, session number; lm_end() stops it
#> Julia 1.12.5 running: 4 threads, LatentMixtures.jl loaded (session 25)
# }
